dependencies.title: A simple and self-contained proof for the Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem
dependencies.locator: Theorem 3.2 (the linear independence of exponentials of distinct algebraic exponents over all algebraic coefficients); Corollary 3.2, printed p.16 (nonzero complex algebraic exponent has transcendental exponential)
dependencies.mapping: For nonzero real algebraic time t, collected finite exponential polynomials with real algebraic frequencies vanish at t exactly when identically zero; used with a separate imaginary-time nonvanishing witness for discriminants, resultants and fixed-model traces. The theorem gives no quantitative lower bound. The algebraic-entry antiunitary corollary uses the same input. TRACE-013 uses only Corollary 3.2 and nonzero algebraic-coefficient polynomials at one transcendental exponential for its factorial flat perturbation. FLOW-013 uses Corollary 3.2 for one eigenvalue rotation, ensuring all positive power traces of its abstract clustered starting family are nonzero without quantitative cancellation. FM-024 uses Theorem 3.2 only for its algebraic-entry literal-propagator corollary: spectral projectors of the Hermitian algebraic generator have algebraic entries even with repeated eigenvalues; entrywise separation of the distinct algebraic exponents forces commutation with both A and M. The common-commutant theorem itself is independent of this external input. Additional scoped use: four finite N=21,35,49,63 U-simplicity cases via prior imaginary-time leading-minor discriminant; one-step squared-trace transcendence for all odd N except7 by collected algebraic difference frequencies and unique extreme coefficient, including repeated eigenvalues. No higher-power seven-divisible conclusion. New rank-transfer use: algebraic matrix-polynomial minors of U(t) are collected exponential polynomials; nonzero real algebraic t realizes maximal rank. Derivative-stack ranks give multiplicity-bounded eigenspace dimensions. Separate fresh FM-008 primary-source/application review verifies its existing spectral uses; its r1 pair-commutant leaf does not require LW. Reviewed intermediate-layer application: add simple local branch counts over disjoint complete newest/first-old/residual25 cat eigenspaces, then apply the existing exponential-rank transfer to give 612N/625+7(even e>=4), 612N/625+175(even e>=6), 4333 at N=4375 and 107443 at N=109375. No fixed-time oldform invariant-subspace or full-simplicity conclusion. Odd newest/residual125 application: disjoint complete cat groups give 24N/25, +35, and +875 total at odd depths e>=3,5,7 respectively; the existing exponential-rank theorem transfers these local branch counts to nonzero real algebraic time. No full simplicity or invariant target-time oldform space.

dependencies.title: Existence of primitive divisors of Lucas and Lehmer numbers
dependencies.pinned_version: Journal fur die reine und angewandte Mathematik 539 (2001), 75-122 (appendix by M. Mignotte)
dependencies.locator: Theorem 1.4 (Section 1): for n > 30 every n-th Lucas number has a primitive divisor; primitive divisor of u_n: p | u_n, p not dividing (alpha-beta)^2 u_1...u_{n-1}. Theorem number corroborated by the publisher abstract and a secondary citation; primary page not pinned (see literature/lineI_sources_20261031.md)
dependencies.mapping: Lucas pair alpha, beta = 1 +- sqrt2 ((P,Q) = (2,-1); alpha+beta = 2, alpha beta = -1 coprime; alpha/beta not a root of unity), u_n = U_n (Pell), V_n = 2h_n. With n = 2m > 30 (m >= 16) a primitive prime p of U_2m is odd (p does not divide 8), divides h_m (U_2m = 2 h_m U_m, p does not divide U_m) and no h_m' with m' < m (h_m' | U_2m'). Used in BGS-TRACE-219 through the hypothesis hBHV of Bgs.LineIArith.finite_set_fails (weaker than Theorem 1.4).

dependencies.title: On the Numerical Factors of the Arithmetic Forms alpha^n +- beta^n
dependencies.locator: Carmichael's theorem on real Lucas sequences (cited as Theorem XXIII by secondary sources; Wikipedia gives Theorem 21): for real non-degenerate Lucas sequences and n not in {1, 2, 6}, U_n has a primitive prime divisor except n = 12, (P,Q) = (+-1,-1). Locator unverified in the primary text
dependencies.dependency_role: corroborating prior result; not load-bearing (EXT-BHV-2001 suffices for the stated range)
dependencies.mapping: (P,Q) = (2,-1) is a real Lucas sequence (D = 8 > 0), so U_2m has a primitive prime for every m >= 2 with 2m != 6; this corroborates, with a smaller threshold, the m >= 16 range of BGS-TRACE-219.

dependencies.title: The Method of Trigonometrical Sums in the Theory of Numbers (equidistribution of (p gamma) mod 1 over the primes, Chapter XI; first announced in Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 15 (1937))
dependencies.identifier: Interscience, London-New York, 1954 (English transl. K. F. Roth, A. Davenport); original announcement Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 15 (1937), 291-294 (Russian); no DOI
dependencies.pinned_version: The Method of Trigonometrical Sums in the Theory of Numbers, Interscience 1954, Chapter XI (as cited in Kuipers-Niederreiter, Uniform Distribution of Sequences, Wiley 1974, Chapter 1 Section 2 Notes: Vinogradov [3, 4; 5, Chapter 11])
dependencies.locator: Statement: for irrational gamma, sum_{p <= x} e(p gamma) = o(pi(x)), equivalently (p_n gamma) is u.d. mod 1. Located through Kuipers-Niederreiter Ch. 1 Sec. 2 Notes (text read) and Davenport GTM 74 2nd ed. Sections 25-26 (contents page); the primary text (Doklady note, Chapter XI of the book) was not read and no page is pinned. Iwaniec-Kowalski Theorem 13.6 is only the minor-arc estimate and is not cited as the full statement
dependencies.mapping: Applied with gamma = H alpha + k/56 (H != 0, k mod 56, alpha = 3 arg xi_2:1/2 pi irrational under H_arg, BGS-TRACE-233) to get sum_{p <= x, p == p0 mod 56} e(p H alpha) = o(pi(x)), hence equidistribution of (p alpha) over p == p0 (mod 56) with EXT-DAVENPORT-1980 and EXT-WEYL-1916; this makes S+ infinite of relative density 0.18001 in BGS-TRACE-231.

additional_uses.scope: Theorem K3 irrational case (Line K): the same application as in BGS-TRACE-231 (u.d. of (p alpha) over p == p0 mod 56), now as one branch of an unconditional case split on arg xi/2 pi; H_arg (BGS-TRACE-233) is not assumed.

dependencies.title: Ueber die Gleichverteilung von Zahlen mod. Eins
dependencies.locator: Weyl criterion: a sequence (x_n) is u.d. mod 1 iff (1/N) sum_{n <= N} e(H x_n) -> 0 for every integer H != 0; textbook form Kuipers-Niederreiter, Uniform Distribution of Sequences (1974), Chapter 1, Theorem 2.1 (text read; KN attribute it to Weyl [2, 4], [4] = this paper). The primary 1916 text was not read; the page of the criterion within pp. 313-352 is not pinned
dependencies.mapping: Applied to the subsequence of primes p == p0 (mod 56) (counting measure normalised by #{p <= x, p == p0}) with x_p = p alpha, alpha = 3 arg xi_2:1/2 pi, to pass from the exponential-sum bound (EXT-VINOGRADOV-1937) to equidistribution and hence to the density arccos(0.84431)/pi = 0.18001 of S+ in BGS-TRACE-231.

additional_uses.scope: Theorem K3 irrational case (Line K): Weyl criterion for the primes p == p0 (mod 56), as in BGS-TRACE-231.

dependencies.title: Multiplicative Number Theory (second edition, revised by Hugh L. Montgomery)
dependencies.pinned_version: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 74, Springer, New York, 2nd ed. 1980
dependencies.locator: Sections 20 and 22, 'The prime number theorem for arithmetic progressions (I), (II)' (pp. 121-125 and 132-134 per the publisher contents page): pi(x; q, a) ~ pi(x)/phi(q) for (a, q) = 1. Section 1 (Dirichlet) gives only infinitude and is not sufficient for the density. Primary text not read; locator from the publisher contents page
dependencies.mapping: Applied with q = 56 and (p0, 56) = 1: #{p <= x : p == p0 mod 56} ~ pi(x)/24, so the normalisation in the equidistribution step of BGS-TRACE-231 is by a positive proportion of all primes and the o(pi(x)) of EXT-VINOGRADOV-1937 suffices.

additional_uses.scope: Theorem K3 irrational case (Line K): normalisation #{p <= x : p == p0 mod 56} ~ pi(x)/24, as in BGS-TRACE-231.

dependencies.title: On Some Exponential Sums
dependencies.pinned_version: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the USA 34 (1948), no. 5, 204-207 (published 15 May 1948; PubMed 16578290; PMC1079093)
dependencies.locator: Estimates for exponential sums attached to a multiplicative character chi of k* and an additive character omega over the rational function field k(t), derived from the Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields; the Kloosterman case |K(a, b; p)| <= 2 sqrt p is derived there. The text of pp. 204-205 (set-up: the character p(m) = omega[R_m(1/T)] chi[R_m(b)], conductor of degree N + d, L-series a polynomial of degree N + d - 2) was read in a search-index text extract; pp. 206-207 (the final estimates) were not read and no equation is pinned. The twisted form |sum_x chi(x) e((ax + b/x)/q)| <= 2 sqrt q (q prime, (a, b) != (0, 0) mod q) used here is the standard consequence; it was not checked against the primary page
dependencies.mapping: Applied in Lemma W1 (BGS-TRACE-241) with q prime, q | h_{3p}, q == +-1 mod 8, H = <l> subset F_q^* of order r(q): detecting H by the characters of F_q^* trivial on H writes sum_{h in H} e((Ah + B/h)/q) as an average of twisted Kloosterman sums (AB != 0; each <= 2 sqrt q) or Gauss sums (AB = 0; modulus sqrt q or 1), giving <= 2 sqrt q (<= sqrt q if AB = 0). Used only through W1 in Lemma W3 and the conditional Theorem W / K2' (BGS-TRACE-243, 245, 246).

Context only (not load-bearing here): the moment inequality (6.6) (re-derived in diagonal form in Line N, Lemma N1.1) and Theorem 2.7 / Corollary 2.9 (S_{2,p}(a, b; A) << min(tau^{23/36} p^{1/6}, tau^{20/27} p^{1/9}), implied constants not stated)

dependencies.title: Weil Sums over Small Subgroups
dependencies.pinned_version: Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 176 (2024), no. 1, 39-53; arXiv:2211.07739 (arXiv text read)
dependencies.locator: Lemma 2.1 (Voloch, Acta Arith. 52 (1989) 197-201, Theorem (i), in the form quoted there): for F absolutely irreducible over F_p of degree d < p, #{F = 0} <= 4 d^{4/3} p^{2/3} + 3p. Voloch's original was not retrieved (cited via this lemma)

dependencies.title: Explicit Bounds on Monomial and Binomial Exponential Sums
dependencies.pinned_version: The Quarterly Journal of Mathematics 62 (2011), no. 2, 323-349
dependencies.locator: Theorem 1.1 (explicit Heath-Brown-Konyagin): for a subgroup A of Z_p^* and (a, p) = 1, max |sum_{x in A} e_p(ax)| <= p^{1/2} for |A| > p^{2/3}/3, <= lambda |A|^{3/8} p^{1/4} for p^{1/2} < |A| <= p^{2/3}/3, and <= lambda |A|^{5/8} p^{1/8} for 3 p^{1/3} < |A| <= p^{1/2}, lambda = 2/3^{1/4} = 1.519671... (ranges checked against the author preprint dated 5 Oct 2009; the published QJM text was not accessible, publisher returned 403 on 2026-10-31)
dependencies.mapping: Proposition N1.3, isotropic x (BGS-TRACE-279): |S|/tau <= min(sqrt q/tau, lambda q^{1/4} tau^{-5/8}, lambda q^{1/8} tau^{-3/8}), lambda = 2/3^{1/4}, each branch only in its range (Gauss period for every tau; middle branch for q^{1/2} < tau <= q^{2/3}/3; 5/8 branch for 3 q^{1/3} < tau <= q^{1/2}); with all three branches the isotropic case covers the whole Theorem W+ range for every p (owner audit of PR #65, R1/R2; integration note I-1; iso_coverage.py). dependencies.title: Mordell's Exponential Sum Estimate Revisited
dependencies.pinned_version: Journal of the American Mathematical Society 18 (2005), no. 2, 477-499 (S 0894-0347(05)00476-5)
dependencies.locator: Theorem 1 and Corollary (1.21): for r >= 1 and eps > 0 there is delta = delta(r, eps) > 0 such that if theta_1, ..., theta_r in F_p^* satisfy ord(theta_i) > p^eps and ord(theta_i theta_j^-1) > p^eps (i != j), then max_{a_i in F_p^*} |sum_{s=1}^{p-1} e_p(sum_i a_i theta_i^s)| < p^{1-delta}; Remark (1) (the case r = 1, Bourgain-Konyagin); section 5(1): delta_r > exp(-C_3 r (eps^-C_2 + log r)) with absolute constants not computed
dependencies.mapping: Line N N2 (BGS-TRACE-281): theta_1 = l, theta_2 = 1/l (orders r, r; ratio order r; r odd, r >= p >= q^{1/C}) give |S(x)| <= (q/(q-1)) q^{-delta(C)} for non-isotropic x at prime q <= p^C; r = 1 for isotropic x; with eps_F of BGS-TRACE-278, Theorem W holds for q, 7q <= p^C and p >= p0(C) = eps_F^{-1/delta(C)}, effective, constants not computed.
